definitions.explanation: People connected by blood, marriage, or other ties — including extended family and in-laws. More formal and broader than just blood relatives.

examples.japanese: {遠|とお}い{縁者|えんじゃ}にあたる。
{親類|しんるい}{縁者|えんじゃ}{一同|いちどう}が{集|あつ}まった。
examples.english: Relatives and connections all gathered together.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}には{頼|たよ}れる{縁者|えんじゃ}が{一人|ひとり}もいない。
examples.english: He has not a single relative he can rely on.

notes:
Compound of {縁|えん} (connection, tie) + {者|じゃ} (person). Formal vocabulary, more often seen in written language or legal/genealogical contexts than in everyday conversation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {親類|しんるい}{縁者|えんじゃ}: relatives and connections (set phrase)
- {遠|とお}い{縁者|えんじゃ}: a distant relation
- {縁者|えんじゃ}にあたる: to be a relation (of someone)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {親戚|しんせき}: relatives — the everyday word; usually blood/marriage relatives
- {親類|しんるい}: relatives — similar to {親戚|しんせき} but slightly more formal
- {身内|みうち}: family; one's own people — emphasizes the inner circle of close kin
